judgements.justification: B's area chair counted at full weight Reviewer_hENG's 7 (confidence 1, 'not a theorist', proofs unread) and Reviewer_DACB's 7 ('cannot ... vouch for the new results'), which lifted B's mean to 7.0 and its spotlight.
A split 2-2 at equal confidence 3, and A's area chair adopted Reviewer_x5V9's positioning critique by name without addressing the 7 and 6; B had no such split.

The authors gave both committees near-identical restructuring promises; the differences (lambda_min fix to A, tightness experiments to B) answered questions only one committee asked and do not conflict.

B's Reviewer_kYKg accepted a 'first convergence proof of a fixed-size deep network' claim that the paper's own Section 7 contradicts with earlier deep-linear GD guarantees, and that novelty view fed kYKg's 7.
B's three-sentence meta-review gives no reason for a spotlight over a poster, and its scores include a 6 and two low-confidence 7s.
A's critics objected as optimization theorists to density, positioning and the comparison with Arora et al., not from the premises of a neighbouring field.
B had Reviewer_4TKP, the most careful review on either side, at 8; A's most positive reviewer, Reviewer_4GXj (7), wrote generic praise and never replied after the rebuttal.
A's detractors rejected the promised rewrite as 'too consequent' (jeQC) with 'little guarantee' it would be done (x5V9), while B's Reviewer_4TKP took the same changes as fixing his concerns.
Both area chairs relied only on the visible reviews and discussion; no off-record assessment appears.
Both committees judged the paper as a theory contribution on the same terms; they differed on presentation and trust in promises, not on the standard for its contribution type.
A's low scores (x5V9 4, jeQC 3) held on positioning, density and the comparison with Arora et al., which are central to the contribution, not peripheral.
